newsitem.title: ISRAEL: Palestinians hail U.N. resolution on settlements.
newsitem.headline: Palestinians hail U.N. resolution on settlements.

text.p: The Palestinian Authority welcomed on Saturday a U.N. resolution calling for an immediate halt to the building of a new Jewish settlement in Arab East Jerusalem.

Palestinian officials said the United States, which voted against the resolution on Friday, was sending its special envoy Dennis Ross to the region in the coming week to try to revive stalled Israeli-Palestinian peace talks.

"President (Yasser) Arafat and the cabinet hailed the U.N. General Assembly's resolution as a great resolution. We hope the message was clear to Israel that it must halt all unilateral steps that damage the peace process," chief Palestinian negotiator Saeb Erekat said.

The General Assembly, at a rare emergency special session that can be resumed, also voted 134-3, with 11 abstentions, for the cessation of all forms of assistance and support for "illegal activities" in the occupid territories. The assembly's decisions are non-binding.

The United States, the main broker in the Arab-Israeli peace process which last month vetoed two Security Council resolutions criticising Israel over the settlements, voted against the General Assembly resolution, along with Israel and Micronesia.
The PLO said it would turn again to the United Nations if Israel continued building the Jewish settlement on Jabal Abu Ghneim, called Har Homa by Israelis, in the occupied part of Jerusalem.

"The U.N. General Assembly has regained its historical role and responsibilities towards the Palestinian cause. Its resolution has given the U.N. the mechanism and the authority to play an effective role to force Israel to respect international legitimacy," the Palestinian Authority said in a statement issued after its weekly Friday meeting.
Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu's spokesman condemned the General Assembly's resolution as an "unconscionable onslaught on a perfectly innocent act by Israel."
Peace talks between Israel and the PLO have been halted since the groundbreaking on Har Homa settlement on March 18.

Ross visited the region earlier this month to try to bring Israelis and Palestinians back to the negotiating table, but the United States said afterwards that major gaps remained between the two sides' positions.
"Dennis Ross will be here on May 2. We are interested in a political decision and solution in order to push the peace process forward," said Arafat's spokesman Marwan Kanafani.
Erekat confirmed that Ross would travel to the region in the coming week.
